### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-datasource`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via SqliteConfigSchema (symbol, a top-level const), SqliteWasmConfigSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/datasources/test (route, a path literal in acceptanceCriteria), /api/v1/meta/datasource/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/meta/datasource/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/datasources/test (route, a path literal in acceptanceCriteria))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4831d5006ded46c123075c43b400c50bfea7d32d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `250448305c63e975fcc29afce153fb16c18d54fc` — the merge of head `5c12bcd442347c3a5d459795f1ccc06a1f9c4fac` into base `4831d5006ded46c123075c43b400c50bfea7d32d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 250448305c63e975fcc29afce153fb16c18d54fc && git checkout 250448305c63e975fcc29afce153fb16c18d54fc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4831d5006ded46c123075c43b400c50bfea7d32d 5c12bcd442347c3a5d459795f1ccc06a1f9c4fac && git checkout -B drift-repro 4831d5006ded46c123075c43b400c50bfea7d32d && git merge --no-ff 5c12bcd442347c3a5d459795f1ccc06a1f9c4fac

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4831d5006ded46c123075c43b400c50bfea7d32d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4831d5006ded46c123075c43b400c50bfea7d32d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The lane remainder at TIER_DEFAULT: the changeset, the new spec test file and the `service-datasource` file are read here as cited code, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set narrowed on `SqliteConfigSchema.filename` and `SqliteWasmConfigSchema.filename` — right, and exactly the ruling plus the scope addition.** Both keys are now `sqliteFilename()` (`sqlite.zod.ts` L91–100, used at L130 and L177). `sqliteFilenameRefusal` (L72–85) refuses exactly two classes: `''`, and any string whose first character is `:` other than the exact string `:memory:` (so `:memory:/srv/data/parts.db`, `:memory:parts.db`, `::memory:`, `:`, and `:MEMORY:` — the last is right too, since SQLite's fileless name is the exact byte string). Every other value is untouched: `:memory:` returns before any arm; an absent key never reaches the refinement because `.default(':memory:')` sits after `.superRefine` (L97); relative, absolute, Windows-drive and `file:` paths and `memory.db` fall through to `undefined`; a whitespace-only name is not refused (the ruling did not ask for it and the admin doors' filesystem arm judges it). The seven alias keys in `FILENAME_ALIASES` (L32–40) are not values of `filename` and were never accepted: `strictObject` answers them `unrecognized_keys` with the rename hint from the `aliases` table, exactly as before; the stored-row rewrite is the D2 conversion `datasource-config-driver-key-aliases`, untouched by this diff. The refinement is placed on top of `placeholderFree` (`common.zod.ts` L777) so a `:${DATA_DIR}/app.db` value reports both issues. `.describe()` / `.meta()` are byte-identical to `main`, so no generated artifact moved (`check:generated` green in `Lint & Repo Gates`).
- **Both doors refuse through the spec schema alone — right.** The metadata door: `getMetadataTypeSchema('datasource')` is `DatasourceSchema` (`metadata-type-schemas.ts` L131, L306–312); `DatasourceSchema`'s `.superRefine` calls `reportDriverConfigIssues(ctx, ds.driver, ds.config, ['config'])` (`datasource.zod.ts` L908), which replays `validateDriverConfig` → `getDriverConfigSchema(driver).safeParse(config)` (`config-registry.zod.ts` L596–614) and re-paths every issue under `config`; the PUT door resolves that schema through `resolveOverlaySchema` (`protocol-meta-type-schema.ts` L556–562) and answers `parseDiagnostics` → `zodIssuesToMetadataIssues` (`metadata-diagnostics.ts` L312–335) as `422 INVALID_METADATA`. The build door: `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.datasources` is `z.array(DatasourceSchema)` (`stack.zod.ts` L763); `os build` parses with it (`compile.ts` L442), `os validate` too (`validate.ts` L375), and `defineStack` raises the same parse as `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` / 422 (`stack.zod.ts` L3633). Neither door has a second copy of the rule.
- **One definition in the service — right.** `assertValidConfig` (`datasource-admin-service.ts` L1415–1426) runs `validateDriverConfig` first, formats each issue as `config.PATH: MESSAGE`, and calls `sqliteDatabaseFilenameIssue` only when that list is empty. The two removed service strings and the two new spec strings are the same sentences, so the admin doors' answers are byte-identical to `main` once the `config.filename: ` prefix is added by the formatter. The filesystem arm (`resolveSqliteAbsentFileTarget(filename, 'empty-in-memory')`, L69–74) is kept. `sqliteDatabaseFilenameIssue` is not exported from the package index and has exactly one caller in the tree, so its precondition ("config already passed its driver contract") is held by the only door that reaches it; no public surface moved. Read, not a finding: if a future caller ever violated that precondition, `resolveSqliteAbsentFileTarget` answers `openedEmptyInMemory: false` for `''` and a `:`-prefixed name (`sql-driver-top-level.ts` L3867–3869) and the judge returns `undefined` — a silent pass, which is the designed cost of holding one copy; the docblock's ⛔ against restating the arms is the right call under PD #12.
- **No runtime boot path is newly refused.** `sqliteFilenameFromUrl` (`standalone-stack.ts` L664) can still produce `:memory:?cache=shared` from `OS_DATABASE_URL=file::memory:?cache=shared`; that value goes to `DefaultDatasourcePlugin` as a driver config (L1022) and the row it publishes to metadata carries `config: {}` by design (`default-datasource-plugin.ts` L263–283), so the spec never judges it on that path. The dev's acceptance note ("refused wherever it is judged against the spec") is accurate and means the two doors only. Both drivers already read a leading `:` as fileless (`sql-driver-database-helpers.ts` L90; `sql-driver-top-level.ts` L3867), so the refused class never opened a file anywhere — the narrowing takes no working capability away from a consumer; it makes the spec's own refusal real at the two doors that lacked it.
- **JSON-Schema projection unchanged — right as scoped.** A `superRefine` does not project, so the driver catalog's `configSchema` (`GET /api/v1/datasources/drivers`) still types `filename` as a plain string; the Setup dialog is refused server-side by the admin doors as before (`sqlite-filename-neither-memory-nor-path.test.ts` L129–175, unchanged, green). A `pattern` would change what `ui/**` validates inline, which the claim fences to `domain:ui#5`; leaving it out is the correct lane discipline.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/30400-sqlite-filename-names-a-database.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/service-datasource` minor; summary line `fix(spec)!: …`; `**BREAKING**` banner; FROM → TO with the one-line fix for both refused classes; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` line-initial in both the changeset body and the PR body; exactly one marker, `adr-0087: registered sqlite-filename-names-no-database-refused`.
- **The declaration is right.** `clause2-line.mjs` (L111–117): `no (narrowing)` is "NOT a widening, but breaking"; `yes (narrowing)` would assert that one surface also widened, and nothing here widens. The card body's "Expected declarations: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`" was the filer's guess; triage 6655226138 and claim 6663609014 carry `no (narrowing)`, which is the spelling the diff earns. A value refused is `narrowed` by AGENTS.md step 3's own list; `narrowed` beside the `(narrowing)` arm satisfies the level gate's contradiction check (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs` header, items 2 and 15–16).

- **The ADR-0087 disposition is the only one the gate admits.** `breakingDeclaration` (`check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` L718–735) reads four signals here (`BREAKING`, `bang`, `clause-②-narrowing`, `metadata-protocol-narrowed`); the body carries a FROM → TO prescription, so `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is refused as a self-contradiction (L147–154); `runtime-interface-only` and `type-surface-only` do not fit a `*.zod.ts` surface; `registered` requires every id to resolve at HEAD and at least one to be new in the diff (L137–139, L5490–5512) — the entry is new here. Amendment 6665827733 widened the claim's file surface to the entry before the review, so the deviation the dev reported is closed. `Lint & Repo Gates` (which runs the gate) on the head: success.

Not filed as a card here, and none is owed by this PR: the dialog user is already refused at Test connection and Save, so the gap is cosmetic until the ui lane picks a projection it can render.
- **Dev flag: `sqliteFilenameFromUrl` can emit a now-refused value.** Answered in ①: that value reaches no spec parse on the standalone boot path, and already opened no file in either driver. Nothing to change in this PR; if a later card wants the runtime to refuse `file::memory:?cache=shared` at boot, that is a `domain:runtime` narrowing of its own.
- **Dev flag: the #30331 changeset's "as before" sentence is superseded.** Right not to edit another card's unreleased changeset; both ship in one release and the later one states the new truth; the release notes are compiled centrally (AGENTS.md, `content/docs/releases/` RELEASE-OWNED).

- **Card expectation `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` vs. the PR's `no (narrowing)`** — resolved in ② in the PR's favour.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/driver/sqlite.zod.ts`** — against triage 6655226138 (a `:`-prefixed value accepted only as exactly `:memory:`), scope addition 6655116984 (`''` too, same prescription, filesystem arm stays in the runtime), and its first consumers (`validateDriverConfig` → `DatasourceSchema` replay → the two doors).

- The refinement implements both asks and nothing more; the message names the value, says why ("A name that starts with ':' is not read as a file, so this datasource would store nothing") and prescribes the fix (exactly `:memory:`, or a file path "with nothing in front of it"), and the `''` arm carries the same prescription. No tracker number in either runtime string; the `#8336` / `#30400` citations are in comments only (`check:doc-authoring` green).
- Tried to break it: `:memory:` with trailing whitespace is refused (right: SQLite would open a file of that name); `file::memory:` (URI form) is accepted as before (a `file:` name is a path to every layer, and the ruling does not reach it); a non-string `filename` is `z.string()`'s `invalid_type`, so the refinement never sees it; the absent key defaults before the refinement; `superRefine` issues do not abort, so the placeholder and the naming refusals compose (pinned: two issues at `filename`). The single builder means the two schemas cannot drift. The JSDoc at L66–70 states the division of labour with the service correctly and names the file that holds the other arm.
- Verdict for this file: holds. No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.sqlite-filename-names-no-database-refused.ts`** — against ADR-0087 D2/D3 (a change with no lossless mapping goes to D3 as a structured TODO with surface, reason, acceptance criteria), `SemanticMigration` (`types.ts` L99–150), and its first consumers (`gen:migration-registry`, `os migrate meta`, the registration gate).

- Filename `18.ID.ts` matches `shardNameFor(18, id)` (`build-migration-registry.ts` L246–256; the registry errors on a mismatch); step 18 is the open protocol major (`PROTOCOL_VERSION = '18.0.0'`). `id` is kebab-case and unique among the 475 step-18 entries. `surface` opens with the dotted path (`data.Datasource.config.filename …`) and names the two authoring routes, the sibling convention. `reason` is the one load-bearing prose field and does its job: it states the failure in each driver and why no mechanical rewrite exists (the ambiguity between the ephemeral intent and the typed path), which is the D2 exclusion stated for this entry. `acceptanceCriteria` is a consumer verify loop (`os validate` clean at `config.filename`, PUT answers 200, Test connection `ok: true` for `:memory:` or an existing file) and is consistent with #27512 (an absent-but-creatable path is refused by Test connection, so it is not promised). No `#NNNN` in any field. No `conversionIds` — right, no D2 edit is judged. `migrations.test.ts` L135–140 (non-empty reason and criteria) is satisfied; `Test Core` on the head: success.
- `relevantWhen` is omitted, and that is the right call by `semantic-relevance.test.ts`'s own criterion (L29–34): the enumerated batch is entries whose surface lives only under top-level stack keys "— no runtime request body, no code door —" and whose criteria send the author to no runtime door. This surface is also reachable through `PUT /api/v1/meta/datasource/NAME`, and its criteria send the author to the PUT and Test doors, so it must stay listed for every stack. Adding one would be a reviewed edit of that table and would wrongly silence the TODO for a stack whose refused datasource lives only in stored metadata.
- Tried to break it: the `replacement` tells the author which of the two fixes keeps data and which does not, so the judgment the entry delegates is decidable from the text alone; the `surface` names `defineStack`, `os validate`, `os build` and the PUT door, all of which ① confirmed parse through `DatasourceSchema`. The registration gate resolves the id in `entries/semantic` at HEAD (L530) and finds it new against the merge base — the `registered` marker is the one honest disposition.
